title: The store survives ungraceful process termination without corrupting on-disk state
description: An abrupt SIGKILL, host power loss, or container OOM-kill of the running process leaves the on-disk store openable on the next boot with every committed write intact and every in-flight transaction rolled back. The store's durability posture (write-ahead log with a synchronous commit floor, or the engine-native equivalent) is set at open time and is not a caller concern.
rationale: A store that corrupts on an ungraceful shutdown is a store that will corrupt in production sooner or later: hosts die, containers get killed, the OOM killer picks the process at 03:00. Making crash safety a store-side default rather than a per-call ceremony means every consumer inherits it without having to remember.
